result.title: Tissot indicatrix for location encoders: Characterizing local distortion in learned geographic embeddings
result.summary: With the increasing adoption of geographic artificial intelligence, location encoders are widely used to map geographic coordinates to learned embeddings for tasks in Earth observation and geospatial modeling. Similar to map projections, location encoders can distort geographic space, that is, equal-distance displacements in different directions can result in unequal embedding changes. However, such distortion remains largely unexamined, and it can propagate into downstream applications. We adapt Tissot's indicatrix, a cartographic tool for map projection distortion, to characterize this distortion. At each location, we compare encoder outputs at equal distances in 32 directions and fit a tensor, represented by an ellipse, whose elongation (anisotropy) and orientation describe the local distortion. The fit requires only encoder outputs without access to model internals and is validated against references with known geometry. By applying the method to thirteen released checkpoints of five encoder families, we find that distortions vary across space and inherit the input geometry to varying degrees, closely in GeoCLIP with its Equal Earth input (anisotropy correlation of 0.88) and weakly or moderately in the other encoders. The distortion also affects the locations an encoder treats as neighbors. Within 1km of 20 query sites, the 40 nearest neighbors in geographic and embedding space overlap by a median of only 57.5--87.5% across the checkpoints, while the fitted ellipses select exactly the same embedding neighbors in 265 of 299 comparisons. These findings provide a geographic basis for assessing location encoders, and the accompanying eTissot package implements the methods for user-specified encoders.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文把地图投影中的 Tissot 指示图改造为位置编码器的局部畸变度量：在每个地点于 32 个方向取等距位移、比较编码器输出并拟合椭圆张量，以伸长率（各向异性）和方向刻画畸变，在已知几何参照上验证后用于 5 个编码器族共 13 个 checkpoint，并考察畸变对「近邻」判定的影响。
AI.relevance_reason: 这种仅依赖输出的黑箱局部度量探针，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 视觉状态的空间几何：等距视觉扰动是否引起等量状态变化、各向异性是否扭曲证据邻域，但需判断其能否迁移到多模态内部状态。
